[OzyBe] I don't think this would be much different from a good quality blender. The blade arrangement looks similar (apart from the heating feature - I did not know people drank their nut milks heated up).
The comment in the video about it being quiet enough to be able to read a book, I very much doubt this as high power blades and blending and 'quiet' just do not go together.
The good comments in the listing seemed to be extremely detailed and extremely complimentary to the product.
I have to admit; I have never tried mung bean milk - not sure that I want to.
[deeevan] That extremely detailed review reads extremely AI generated. A few comments mention it not matching the product images, with different buttons/functions. Anyway, I'm after a cheap blender so not fussed if this fails to make nut milk.
I got to say "nut milk maker" multiple times to my partner to OK the purchase, +1 for that.
[StevieRay] Absolutely can do this with a good blender.
Most nut milks are/should be brewed cold.
I believe soy needs to be boiled.
My plan is to prepare at night to allow overnight soaking and set delay so it is operating as I wake up in the morning.
[jeffr] yes soy milk must be boiled as soy beans are legumes and without cooking tastes bitter and terrible! Once cooked the flavour changes and tastes like a fresh soy milk.
It's hard to go back to UHT soy milk after drinking fresh soy milk (which contains all sorts of ingrediants to get the texture).
[BrownManWalking] Got one thanks… My protein blender died and this looks like just any other blender. Nonetheless happy to take a punt for $30..
[Hugh G Rection] I don't need to buy a machine to make nut milk, but the taste varies depending on a few factors.
[ne-us] Thanks op, if it doesn’t work I can use this as a back up blended for $30. 👍
[jeffr] I already have an old school version which I purchased when I was in China. It looks like a normal kettle but it has an element and Bamix like blade. The top of the unit has a few settings so you can make different types of nut milk and it certainly does the job. I've even made tofu from fresh soy bean milk.
Method
250g soy beans soaked over night 6 to 8 hrs. (Buy beans from any Asian grocer)
Remove loose shells
Add to machine and cook until done then sieve/squeeze through a nut cloth or muslin. If the cloth is too dense find one with larger holes - best place to try is Spotlight.
You can make up to 4 and a half cups of soy milk depending how you like the taste - add sugar to taste. Will keep for 2 to 3 days in the refrigerator (max).
If you dont have a nut milk machine - the manual method is to blend the soaked beans using a bamix/blender and then strain and then bring to the boil. Once boiled, let cool and then refrigerate.

I do love it though.
